headline: Fastest streetlight fixes in the city pair with heavy industrial exposure in Ward 11.
summary:
No ward in Chicago closes a broken streetlight request faster than Ward 11, averaging 1.48 days. That speed helps push the ward to 13th of 50 overall, solidly in the top third of the city. Ward 11 sits on the Near South Side and covers Bridgeport, Armour Square, New City, and McKinley Park. Restaurants skew independent too, with a smaller share of chain outlets than anywhere else in Chicago, and grocery access ranks second best citywide.

Ward 11's problems cluster around industry. It sits last among the fifty on proximity to sites with hazardous-chemical risk management plans, and lags most of Chicago on nearby major-emitter facilities, diesel particulate matter in the air, and traffic exposure near homes. All four measures point toward heavier industrial exposure than the rest of Chicago sees.
reading_the_rankings: Two figures here deserve a second look before they carry full weight. The 1st-place mark on streetlight repair time, 1.48 days on average, is real, though this particular count isn't tracked in every one of Chicago's fifty wards, so fewer than fifty are actually being compared. The last-place mark on proximity to hazardous risk management plan sites carries more caveats. Confidence on this particular figure is graded medium by the agency that publishes it, and the number was carved up by acreage, not by a household count, so a tract that straddles the ward line hands part of its total to the neighbors. Most of the fifty aren't far apart here either, the middle twenty-five wards on this measure span just eleven points, so last place is not necessarily far from fortieth. The chain-restaurant figure, 1st place at only six percent of the ward's restaurants tied to a major chain, carries none of those caveats and holds up without qualification.

news.headline: City Worker Who Improved Bike Infrastructure Killed While Biking In Bridgeport
news.note: Riley O'Neil, a Chicago Department of Transportation planner who worked on bike infrastructure, was fatally struck while biking on Halsted Street in Bridgeport.

news.headline: Bridgeport's First Big Street Fest In Years Kicks Off This Weekend With Motoblot
news.note: The motorcycle-themed festival Motoblot moved to Halsted Street in Bridgeport for its first large-scale run in the neighborhood in several years.

news.headline: 42 Parks On South, West Sides Getting Improved Air Conditioning To Help Battle Heat Waves
news.note: Armour Square Park is one of 30 South and West Side parks slated for air conditioning upgrades this summer under a Chicago Park District effort.

news.headline: 'Moving Archer Forward' Initiative Aims To Bring 800 New Housing Units To Archer Avenue
news.note: A city plan would overhaul streets and add about 800 housing units and 280,000 square feet of retail along Archer Avenue from Bridgeport to Garfield Ridge, and heads to the City Council's plan commission next month.
